chunks: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Salim ibn al-Fudhayl, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "We have entered for an Umrah, so should we trim or should we shave?"
So he said: "Shave, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله invoked mercy upon those who shave three times, and upon those who trim only once."

key_terms.الْمُقَصِّرِينَ: those who shorten or trim their hair
key_terms.بِعُمْرَةٍ: for Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage rite
key_terms.تَرَحَّمَ: invoked mercy and supplicated for mercy
key_terms.فَنُقَصِّرُ: should we trim the hair as part of concluding the rite

ai.seo_question: In Umrah, is it better to shave the head or trim the hair?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal preference in the rites of Umrah between trimming the hair and shaving the head. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام instructs shaving, citing the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who prayed for those who shaved three times and for those who trimmed once.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2948 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Salim ibn al-Fudhayl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as): "We have entered Mecca for Umrah. Should we trim (taqsir) or shave (halq)?"
Imam (as) said: "Shave, for the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) invoked mercy for those who shave their heads three times and for those who trim their hair only once."
